title: Domain-aware replay sampling for quantization calibration (INT8/FP8)
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: produce per-domain calibration packs that maximize calibration efficacy for both INT8 and FP8 quantization profiles while keeping pack sizes bounded for runtime cost. This ticket defines a domain-aware replay sampling approach that blends production traffic representativeness, template coverage, and edge-case amplification for robust accuracy validation.

Problem background: current calibration packs are either uniformly sampled from logs (overrepresenting high-volume customers/templates) or hand-curated, leading to poor coverage of tail templates and domain drift that causes quantized models (INT8/FP8) to regress on low-frequency behaviors. We need an automated pipeline to create reproducible per-domain packs with explicit quality guarantees and measurable sampling provenance.

High-level approach: generate per-domain calibration packs by: (1) computing a representativeness score for each production prompt using client-embedded vectors + frequency and recentness; (2) bucketing prompts by template fingerprint, token-length, and interactive vs. batch mode; (3) applying reservoir + stratified replay sampling with controllable tail-boosting and adversarial amplification knobs; (4) budget allocation per quant profile (INT8 vs FP8) and per-domain SLO; (5) include a small synthetic augmentation stage (paraphrases) only for domains with insufficient examples, gated by privacy filters and human review. The pipeline will output metadata for each sampled item (source timestamp, template id, client id hash, score, sampling weight) for audit and reproducibility.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline can produce per-domain calibration packs (JSONL) for at least 8 production domains using last 30 days of logs
Each pack includes sampling metadata and stable pack_id that reproduces the exact set when re-run with the same seed
INT8 and FP8 profile budgets are honored (configurable pack size; default: 2k examples for INT8, 1k for FP8 per domain)
Validation harness runs compare quantized outputs to FP16 baseline and produce token-level KL/divergence, generation-accuracy delta (sequence-level), and regression report
Pipeline integrates with CI to fail PRs if median KL > 0.02 or >1% of prompts exceed sequence-level regression threshold for a domain
progress_log: 2026-02-18: RFC drafted — outlined scoring formula combining embedding similarity (client-specific centroid), recency weight (exponential decay), and token-length stratification.
2026-02-23: Spike completed — prototype sampler (Python) that implements reservoir sampling per-template and global tail-boosting; demoed with 3 domains (search, chat, summarization).
2026-03-02: Feedback from PM (J. Chen) — add privacy gating and reduce paraphrase rate. Added privacy filter module to pipeline design.
2026-03-05: Eng review — Miguel and S. Ramesh validated reproducibility by seeding; discovered nondeterminism in embedding indexing; switched to disk-based l2 index with deterministic sharding.

2026-03-09: Initial calibration runs — produced packs for 8 domains; INT8 run showed median token KL=0.018 vs FP16 baseline (target <0.02); FP8 comfortably under threshold. Detailed results in validation_results field.
2026-03-10: Preparing infra PR for scheduled job + CI gating; lockdown of sampling knobs pending security review.
decisions: Use client-agnostic hashed client_id in metadata to preserve privacy while allowing per-client skew analysis
Default pack sizes: INT8=2000 examples/domain, FP8=1000 examples/domain. These are configurable properties in the pipeline config.
Synthetic paraphrases allowed only when domain has <10 unique templates in window; paraphrase rate capped at 20% and routed to a human-review queue for high-risk domains
Sampling pipeline will emit a deterministic pack_id computed from seed + window + domain so packs are reproducible for audits
tradeoffs: Larger packs improve calibration coverage but increase quant-compile and runtime validation cost — therefore we cap packs per profile and provide per-domain override for high-risk SLAs
Embedding-based scoring is more representative than raw frequency but requires additional compute and a deterministic index; we accept the infra complexity for better tail coverage
Paraphrase augmentation increases coverage but risks introducing distribution shift; limited augmentation and human-review mitigates risk
testing_plan: Unit tests for sampling logic (template bucketing, reservoir, tail-boost) with deterministic seeds
End-to-end pipeline test against a sanitized 30-day production sample: verify pack size, reproducibility, and metadata correctness

Validation harness runs: deploy INT8 and FP8 quantized variants on CI GPUs, compare to FP16 baseline across metrics (token KL, top-1 token accuracy delta, sequence-level generation similarity), and publish a regression dashboard
Canary: run calibration packs on one dedicated capacity pool and monitor latency/cost and any production errors before wide rollout
validation_results: Initial CI validation (2026-03-09): INT8 pack medians: token-KL=0.018, 95p token-KL=0.041; sequence-level regression (BLEU-style similarity proxy) median delta=0.7% with 0.9% prompts > regression-threshold. FP8 medians: token-KL=0.010, 95p=0.022. Conclusion: FP8 passes current thresholds; INT8 is borderline but acceptable for non-high-risk domains. Follow-ups: run another calibration round with tail-boost=1.5 for two worst domains and re-evaluate.
notes_and_followups: Schedule security review for sampled metadata schema (P0) — must ensure client hash scheme is compliant with privacy policy
Add a lightweight dashboard in Console showing per-domain calibration pack composition (template coverage, token-length distribution)
Explore automatic threshold tuning per-domain using historical calibration regression outcomes (future work)
